text: The Fed under Chair Warsh is now signaling possible rate hikes in 2026 with inflation stuck at 3.4% and a blowout jobs report — this means borrowing costs could rise further, which is especially painful for your speculative, cash-burning holdings like QBTS, IONQ, and RGTI.

RGTI is down 42.6% with shrinking revenue, cash burn, insider selling, and 18% short interest — the thesis is broken, and in a rising-rate environment speculative names like this get punished hardest, so exit now to stop the bleeding.

QBTS is down 36.6% with no earnings, 22% short interest, and insiders selling — reduce your exposure because this speculative quantum bet has too much working against it, especially with rates potentially heading higher.

IONQ is down 18% and 51% off its high with a negative PE and speculative quantum computing thesis — trim to a size you can stomach losing entirely, because 202% revenue growth means nothing if the company keeps burning cash in a tightening environment.

Adobe at a PE of 9.1 with nearly 10% free cash flow yield is genuinely cheap for a profitable software giant — this looks like the market is mispricing a quality company, making it worth adding to on this weakness.

Google at a PE of 23 with 15% revenue growth and strong free cash flow is one of the most reasonably priced big tech names you own — worth adding a bit here since profitable companies with real earnings hold up better if rates rise.
